paper_title: Mechanistic Understanding and Mitigation of Language Confusion in   English-Centric Large Language Models
caption: Distribution of Important Neurons Associated with Confusion Points in Llama3-8B. (a) Distribution of the top 300 most important FFN neurons across layers for an individual Chinese prompt “UTF8gbsn请解释拆东墙补西墙的意思。(Please explain `UTF8gbsn拆东墙补西墙.')” from Aya. (b) Aggregated distribution of important neuron scores across all Chinese test samples in Aya.
model_annotation: The two-panel line chart illustrates the distribution of important feed-forward network (FFN) neurons across layers in the Llama3-8B model, specifically for Chinese-language prompts from the Aya dataset. Both subplots share a common x-axis labeled “layer,” which is linearly scaled from 0 to 35 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and a y-axis labeled “count,” which is linearly scaled but with different ranges: 0 to 100 in panel (a) and 0 to 175 in panel (b). In panel (a), titled “Individual Case,” a single blue line with circular markers represents the count of top 300 most important FFN value neurons for one specific Chinese prompt. The line remains near zero from layer 0 to layer 14, then rises gradually to approximately 5–10 through layer 25, dips slightly at layer 26, and then increases sharply from layer 27 to layer 31, reaching a final value of approximately 80. In panel (b), titled “Aggregated Neuron Scores,” a green line with circular markers shows the aggregated neuron importance scores across all Chinese test samples. This line stays near zero from layer 0 to layer 13, remains at approximately 5 from layer 14 to layer 26, dips slightly at layer 27, then rises sharply from layer 28 to layer 31, reaching approximately 60, and continues climbing steeply to approximately 175 at layer 32.

model_annotations.English: The figure presents two line plots illustrating the distribution of important feed-forward network (FFN) neurons associated with confusion points in the Llama3-8B model, specifically for Chinese prompts from the Aya dataset. Both plots share a common x-axis labeled “layer,” ranging from 0 to 35 with tick marks at intervals of 5, and a y-axis labeled “count,” which is linearly scaled but with different ranges: 0 to 100 in plot (a) and 0 to 175 in plot (b). In plot (a), titled “Individual Case,” a single blue line with circular markers represents the count of top 300 most important FFN value neurons for a specific Chinese prompt. The count remains near zero through layers 0 to 15, then fluctuates slightly between 0 and 10 up to layer 25, followed by a sharp increase starting around layer 27, peaking at approximately 95 neurons in layer 31. In plot (b), titled “Aggregated Neuron Scores,” a green line with circular markers shows the aggregated neuron importance scores across all Chinese test samples. This line remains near zero from layer 0 to 27, then rises sharply, reaching approximately 60 at layer 30 and exceeding 175 by layer 32, indicating a strong concentration of important neurons in the final layers when aggregated across multiple samples.
